sourceHtml:
Google Deepmind is making its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video-generation model generally available. The updated model creates clips up to 15 seconds long, supports conversational editing, and costs 30 percent less than its predecessor.

Google says Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is rolling out through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, the Google Cloud Console, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and Google Ads. Every generated video carries an imperceptible SynthID watermark to indicate its origin.

Clips can now run between three and 15 seconds, up from a maximum of 10 seconds previously, and pricing drops 30 percent to $0.07 per second for 720p video. Generated clips can also be edited through an ongoing conversation.

A standout feature is what Google calls "Conversational Editing." Users can tweak a generated clip step by step, changing the background, lighting, or aspect ratio without regenerating the entire clip. Google says this works across the full 15-second length. Paired with a tiered workflow, the feature is supposed to cut costs. Drafts are first created at 360p or 720p, individual details are corrected with a follow-up edit, and only the final result is upscaled to 1080p or 4K.

Google promises more consistent results with reference images

Google also promises significantly better reference adherence. According to the announcement, the model can take character images, product photos, short motion clips of up to three seconds, and audio cues as inputs. Faces, clothing, packaging typography, and brand colors are supposed to stay consistent across different camera angles.

As an example, Google shows a virtual try-on clip. From a single model photo and product shots of three outfits, the model generates a 15-second sequence with 360-degree turns while preserving the model's identity and each garment's cut and drape.

Overall visual consistency is said to have improved as well. Google says there is less visual drift or morphing across motion and camera transitions than with the predecessor.

Beyond that, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is supposed to produce more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue with clearer lip-sync and the ability to distinguish between multiple speakers. The model further handles complex, continuous camera movements such as FPV drone flights or dramatic zoom-outs, with significantly fewer unwanted jump cuts.

translation.html:
Google Deepmind 正式向所有用户开放其 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 视频生成模型。更新后的模型可生成最长 15 秒的视频片段，支持对话式编辑，成本比上一代降低 30%。

Google 表示，Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 正通过 Gemini API、Google AI Studio、Google Cloud Console、Flow、Google Vids、面向 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户的 Gemini 应用以及 Google Ads 逐步推出。每个生成的视频都带有不可感知的 SynthID 水印，用于标明其来源。

视频片段的时长现在可为 3 至 15 秒，此前最长为 10 秒；720p 视频的价格降低 30%，降至每秒 0.07 美元。生成的视频片段还可以通过持续对话进行编辑。

一项突出的功能是 Google 所称的“对话式编辑”。用户可以逐步调整生成的视频片段，更改背景、光照或画面比例，无需重新生成整个片段。Google 表示，这项功能适用于完整的 15 秒视频。配合分阶段工作流程，这项功能旨在降低成本。用户先以 360p 或 720p 生成初稿，再通过后续编辑修正个别细节，最后仅将最终结果提升至 1080p 或 4K。

Google 承诺借助参考图像实现更一致的生成结果

Google 还承诺显著提高对参考素材的遵循程度。根据公告，该模型可以接受人物图像、产品照片、最长 3 秒的简短动作视频片段以及音频提示作为输入。面孔、服装、包装上的字体排版和品牌颜色应能在不同拍摄角度下保持一致。

Google 展示了一段虚拟试衣视频作为示例。仅凭一张模特照片和三套服装的产品照片，该模型便生成了一段包含 360 度转身动作的 15 秒视频，同时保留模特的身份特征，以及每件服装的剪裁和垂坠感。

据称，整体视觉一致性也有所改善。Google 表示，与上一代相比，在动作和镜头转换过程中，视觉漂移或形变更少。

此外，Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 据称能够生成更流畅、听起来更自然的对话，口型同步更清晰，并且能够区分多位说话者。该模型还能够处理复杂、连续的镜头运动，例如第一人称视角（FPV）无人机飞行或大幅拉远镜头，同时显著减少不必要的跳切。
